preparing
fixing
exercises.tip: Si el verbo termina en -e, la e se va: make → making, no «makeing».

exercises.answer: We are sitting in the park.
exercises.tip: sit termina en vocal + consonante: la t se dobla, sitting (igual que shop → shopping). Y «estamos sentados» en inglés es are sitting.

accept: I'm not watching television.
exercises.tip: Para negar, not va después de am/is/are: I'm not watching.

accept: Is your brother working now?
Is your brother working right now?
exercises.tip: Para preguntar se da la vuelta: Is + sujeto + -ing. Sin do.

theory.title: Los dos presentes, y cómo elegir
theory.body:
El inglés tiene dos presentes y cada uno dice algo distinto.

**Presente simple** — lo que haces siempre, tu rutina, lo que es verdad en general:
*I **work** in a bank.* (ese es mi trabajo)
*She **drinks** coffee.* (le gusta el café)

**Presente continuo** — lo que pasa ahora mismo, hoy, esta temporada:
*I **am working** today.* (hoy, en este momento)
*She **is drinking** coffee.* (la taza está en su mano)

Palabras que te avisan: *always, usually, every day* → simple. *now, right now, at the moment* → continuo.

Ojo con *today*: va con los dos. *I am working today* (hoy estoy en eso) y *I work today* (hoy me toca turno) son normales.
theory.trap: Hay verbos que en inglés **casi nunca** van en continuo: like, want, need, know, understand. *I am needing a coffee* ❌ → **I need a coffee** ✅. Expresan un estado (lo que sabes, quieres o necesitas), no una acción.

options: I am working in a bank.
accept: I work at a bank.
I work for a bank.
exercises.tip: Es tu trabajo de siempre, no lo que haces ahorita: presente simple.

accept: I need some coffee.
I need coffee.
exercises.tip: need no se pone en continuo: I need, no I am needing.

exercises.audio: He usually takes the bus.
options: He is usually taking the bus.
exercises.tip: usually avisa que es rutina: presente simple con -s.

exercises.audio: I am watching a movie.
exercises.tip: Ahora mismo, con la película puesta: continuo.
understand expresa un estado: no va en continuo.

exercises.audio: We are waiting for the bus.
exercises.meaning: Estamos esperando el bus.
exercises.tip: Si dices qué esperas, va for: wait for the bus. Sin eso va solo: Please wait.

exercises.text: I don't understand the question.
exercises.tip: Frase útil de verdad. Dila entera y sin prisa.

exercises.text: He is speaking Spanish.
exercises.tip: speaking y Spanish: las dos empiezan con s pura, sin e.

exercises.text: I ___ a new phone.
exercises.tip: want expresa un estado: no va en continuo.

exercises.es: Trabajo en un banco, pero hoy estoy trabajando en casa.
exercises.answer: I work in a bank, but today I'm working at home.
accept: I work at a bank, but today I'm working at home.
I work in a bank, but today I'm working from home.
I work at a bank, but today I'm working from home.
I work in a bank, but I'm working at home today.
I work at a bank, but I'm working at home today.
I work in a bank, but I'm working from home today.
I work at a bank, but I'm working from home today.
I work for a bank, but today I'm working from home.
I work for a bank, but today I'm working at home.
I work for a bank, but I'm working at home today.
I work for a bank, but I'm working from home today.
exercises.tip: Los dos presentes en una frase: la rutina con work, el hoy con am working.

exercises.text: I don't understand the question.
exercises.tip: Frase de cinco palabras. El peso en «STAND» y en «QUES-tion».

exercises.text: She ___ every day.
exercises.tip: every day es rutina → presente simple, con -s para she: cooks.

exercises.text: She ___ right now.
accept: 's cooking
exercises.tip: right now es este momento → is + -ing: is cooking.

exercises.es: Mi papá lee el periódico todas las mañanas.
exercises.answer: My dad reads the newspaper every morning.
accept: My father reads the newspaper every morning.
My dad reads the paper every morning.
My father reads the paper every morning.
Every morning my dad reads the newspaper.
Every morning my father reads the newspaper.
Every morning my dad reads the paper.
Every morning my father reads the paper.
exercises.tip: every morning es una costumbre: presente simple (reads), no is reading.

exercises.es: En este momento estoy hablando por teléfono.
options: At the moment I talk on the phone.
At the moment I am talking on the phone.
At the moment I am talk on the phone.
exercises.answer: At the moment I am talking on the phone.
accept: I am talking on the phone at the moment.
Right now I am talking on the phone.
I am talking on the phone right now.
I am on the phone right now.
I am on the phone at the moment.
At the moment I am speaking on the phone.
I am speaking on the phone at the moment.
Right now I am on the phone.
At the moment I am on the phone.
exercises.tip: at the moment avisa: continuo (am talking). Y «por teléfono» es on the phone.

theory.title: this, that, these, those
theory.body:
Solo hay dos preguntas: ¿está cerca o lejos? ¿es uno o son varios?

| | cerca | lejos |
|---|---|---|
| **uno** | this | that |
| **varios** | these | those |

***This** is my phone.* (lo tengo en la mano)
***That** is your car.* (está allá)
***These** are my keys.* (aquí)
***Those** are his books.* (allá)

Al teléfono se usa así: *Hi, **this** is Fero.*
theory.trap: these y this suenan casi igual y se confunden al escribir. Truco: **these** tiene la e larga de *cheese*, y es la del plural. Además, ojo con la th: no es «dis» ni «zis».

accept: This is my cell phone.
This is my cellphone.
This is my telephone.
exercises.tip: Uno solo y cerca: this.

accept: Those are her keys.
Those are their keys.
Those are your keys.
exercises.tip: Varias y lejos: those. Y el verbo va en plural, are.

exercises.audio: These are my books.
exercises.tip: these + are, siempre juntos en plural.

exercises.audio: That is a good idea.
exercises.tip: idea lleva a delante: a good idea.
Varios y lejos: those, con are.

exercises.audio: This is not my bag.
exercises.meaning: Este no es mi bolso.
exercises.tip: this is not, o this isn't.

exercises.text: This is my brother.
exercises.tip: La th de this: lengua entre los dientes y con voz. No es «dis».

exercises.text: These are my books, and those are yours.
exercises.tip: Dos th: these y those. Lengua entre los dientes en las dos.

exercises.text: ___ are my keys.
exercises.tip: Varias y cerca: these. Y con are, no is.

accept: That's my phone.
That is my cell phone.
That is my cellphone.
That is my telephone.
exercises.tip: Uno solo y lejos: that.

exercises.text: This is my brother.
exercises.tip: Empieza con th sonora. Suena «DHIS-is-my-BRO-ther», sin cortar.
think saca la lengua; sink no. Si dices «sink» estás diciendo «lavaplatos».

exercises.text: I like ___ shirt.
exercises.tip: this también va delante de una cosa: this shirt, this phone.

accept: Those books are really expensive.
exercises.tip: Plural y lejos: those books. Nunca «that books».
Una casa aquí: this house is. these es para varias.

units.title: En la tienda
units.subtitle: Contar, pedir con would like y usar can

theory.title: Cosas que se cuentan y cosas que no
theory.body:
El inglés separa las cosas en dos grupos y usa palabras distintas para cada uno.

**Se cuentan** (apples, chairs, people):
*How **many** apples?* · *a **few** apples* · *some apples*

**No se cuentan** (water, money, time, rice):
*How **much** water?* · *a **little** water* · *some water*

**a lot of** sirve para los dos: *a lot of apples, a lot of water*.

Y en preguntas y negativos, **some** se vuelve **any**:
*I have **some** money.* → *Do you have **any** money?* → *I don't have **any** money.*

Excepción: al ofrecer o pedir algo se queda **some**: *Would you like **some** tea?* · *Can I have **some** water?*
theory.trap: *How many money do you have?* es el error clásico: en español «cuánto dinero» y «cuántas manzanas» se parecen demasiado. El dinero no se cuenta en inglés — se cuentan los billetes, no el dinero. Es **How much money**.

options: How many money do you have?
How much money do you have?
How much moneys do you have?
exercises.answer: How much money do you have?
exercises.tip: money no se cuenta: much. Y nunca lleva -s.
people ya es plural: many. Y en la pregunta, are va antes de there.

exercises.audio: I don't have any sugar.
exercises.tip: En negativo, some se convierte en any.

exercises.audio: There is a lot of water.
options: There are a lot of water.
There is a lot of water.
exercises.answer: There is a lot of water.
exercises.tip: water no se cuenta: is, y a lot of.
En pregunta va any. Y time así no lleva -s.

exercises.audio: We need some milk.
exercises.meaning: Necesitamos leche.
exercises.tip: En afirmativo va some. milk no lleva -s.

exercises.text: How much does this cost?
exercises.tip: La h de How se sopla. Es la pregunta más útil de una tienda.

exercises.text: I need some sugar.
exercises.tip: sugar no suena «su-gar»: es «SHU-gar», con sh.

exercises.text: How ___ money do you need?
exercises.tip: El dinero no se cuenta en inglés: much. Se cuentan los billetes, no el dinero.

accept: I have no sugar.
I don't have sugar.
exercises.tip: En negativo, some se vuelve any. Y sugar nunca lleva -s.

exercises.text: How much does this cost?
exercises.tip: La pregunta de cualquier tienda. Suena «how MUCH does this COST», en dos golpes.
much lleva una vocal central y relajada, entre la a y la o; match lleva la a bien abierta y estirada hacia adelante («mætch»).

exercises.text: I have ___ friends here.
exercises.tip: Cosas que se cuentan (amigos) → a few. a little es para las que no se cuentan.

exercises.text: I need ___ milk.
accept: some
a bit of
a little bit of
exercises.tip: La leche no se cuenta → a little milk, no «a few milk».

exercises.answer: How much water do you drink a day?
accept: How much water do you drink per day?
How much water do you drink every day?
How much water do you drink each day?
How much water do you drink daily?
How much water do you drink in a day?
exercises.tip: El agua no se cuenta → How much water, nunca «How many water». «Al día» es a day.

accept: I have some time.
I have a bit of time.
I have a little bit of time.
exercises.tip: time (tiempo) no se cuenta: a little time. «a few times» sería «unas pocas veces», otra cosa.

theory.title: would like: pedir sin sonar brusco
theory.body:
**I want** no está mal, pero suena seco, como un niño exigiendo. Para pedir cosas se usa:

**I would like** = quisiera (casi siempre escrito **I'd like**)

*I'd like a coffee, please.*
*I'd like to see the menu.*

Y para ofrecer:
**Would you like** a coffee? = ¿quiere un café?
**Would you like** something **to** drink? = ¿quiere algo de beber?

Regla: si va un verbo después, lleva **to**.
*I'd like **to** go.* · *Would you like **to** sit down?*
theory.trap: *I want a coffee* en una cafetería suena a orden. No es gramática, es educación — y en inglés se nota más que en español, donde «quiero un café» pasa sin problema. Di **I'd like a coffee, please**.

options: Would you like something to drink?
exercises.answer: Would you like something to drink?
accept: Would you like anything to drink?
Would you like a drink?
Do you want something to drink?
Would you like to drink something?
Would you like to drink anything?
Do you want anything to drink?
exercises.tip: Para ofrecer: Would you like. Y drink lleva to delante.

options: I'd like to see the menu.
exercises.answer: I'd like to see the menu.
accept: I'd like to look at the menu.
exercises.tip: Si sigue un verbo, hace falta to.

exercises.audio: Would you like some tea?
exercises.tip: Al ofrecer se usa some, aunque sea pregunta. Es la excepción al any.

exercises.audio: She would like to go home.
options: She would like to go home.
exercises.answer: She would like to go home.
exercises.tip: would like to + verbo.

exercises.answer: We'd like a table for two.
exercises.tip: We'd like = we would like. Aquí no hay verbo después, así que no lleva to.

exercises.audio: Would you like to sit down?
exercises.meaning: ¿Quiere sentarse?
exercises.tip: sit down, dos palabras.

exercises.text: I'd like the check, please.
exercises.tip: I'd suena «aid», una sílaba. Tu frase al terminar de comer.

exercises.text: Would you like to sit here?
exercises.tip: La h de here se sopla.

exercises.text: I'd like ___ see the menu.
exercises.tip: Si después de would like va un verbo, lleva to.

exercises.es: Quisiéramos una mesa para dos, por favor.
exercises.answer: We'd like a table for two, please.
accept: We would like a table for two, please.
We'd like a table for two people, please.
We would like a table for two people, please.
exercises.tip: Aquí no hay verbo después, así que no lleva to.

exercises.text: I'd like to see the menu, please.
exercises.tip: I'd suena «aid», una sílaba. El peso en «MENU» y «PLEASE».

theory.title: can: una sola forma para todo
theory.body:
**can** es de los más fáciles del inglés porque **no cambia nunca**.

*I can · you can · he can · she can · we can · they can*

Sin -s, sin do, sin nada.

**Negativo:** can't (*I can't swim.*)
**Pregunta:** Can you...? (*Can you help me?*)

Y lo que va después siempre es el verbo pelado, **sin to**:
*I can **swim**.* · *Can you **help** me?*

También sirve para **pedir permiso**: *Can I sit here?* · *Can I use your phone?*
theory.trap: *He cans* ❌ y *Can you to help me?* ❌ son los dos errores. En español «poder» se conjuga («puedo, puedes, puede») y lleva infinitivo detrás, así que la mano quiere escribir to. En inglés can se queda quieto y lo que sigue va desnudo: **Can you help me?**

accept: Could you help me?
exercises.tip: Después de can, el verbo va sin to.

accept: She speaks three languages.
exercises.tip: can no lleva -s, y el verbo detrás tampoco.

exercises.audio: I can't hear you.
exercises.tip: can't es la negación. Frase de oro en una llamada.

exercises.audio: Can I pay with a card?
options: Can I to pay with a card?
Can I pay with a card?
Do I can pay with a card?
exercises.answer: Can I pay with a card?
exercises.tip: Con tarjeta: with a card o by card, las dos sirven.
can't + verbo pelado.

exercises.audio: Can you say that again?
exercises.meaning: ¿Puede repetir eso?
exercises.tip: Guárdala: te salva cuando no entiendes algo.

exercises.text: Can you help me, please?
exercises.tip: help con la h soplada. «Elp» no se entiende.

exercises.text: Can you speak more slowly?
exercises.tip: speak y slowly empiezan con s pura: nada de «espeak» ni «eslowly».

exercises.text: Can you ___ me?
exercises.tip: Después de can, el verbo va desnudo: sin to y sin -s.

accept: He can play guitar.
He knows how to play the guitar.
He knows how to play guitar.
exercises.tip: can no cambia nunca, y lo que sigue va sin to y sin -s.

exercises.text: Can you speak more slowly?
exercises.tip: Guárdala para cuando te hablen rápido. Sube el tono al final.
Aquí la palabra suena sola: fíjate en la t final de can't, aunque sea corta. En una frase, can suena débil («kn») y can't fuerte. Al decirla tú, marca la t.

accept: May I open the window?
Could I open the window?
exercises.tip: Para pedir permiso: Can I…? y el verbo sin to.

options: Can I to use your phone?
Do I can use your phone?
accept: May I use your phone?
Could I use your phone?
Can I use your cell phone?
Can I borrow your phone?
exercises.tip: can no usa do para preguntar: Can I…?, nunca «Do I can…?».
«Sentarme» es solo sit: el «me» del español no pasa al inglés.

units.title: Precios, gustos y planes
units.subtitle: How much is it?, like + -ing y cómo invitar

theory.title: How much is it? y los plurales con are
theory.body:
Para preguntar el precio: **How much is it?** (una cosa) · **How much are they?** (varias). También: *How much **does** it cost?*

Se responde con el mismo verbo: *It's twelve dollars.* · *They're twenty dollars.*

*$12.50* se dice **twelve fifty** o **twelve dollars and fifty cents**. En pesos: *fifty thousand pesos* (50.000); **thousand** no lleva -s después de un número. Y para opinar: *That's **expensive**.* · *That's **cheap**.*

Los plurales llevan **are**: *These shoes **are** cheap.* Ojo con los irregulares: **person → people** · **child → children** · **man → men** · **woman → women**. *People* ya es plural: ❌ *the peoples* (*peoples* solo existe como «pueblos, naciones»).
theory.trap: De «¿cuánto cuesta?» sale *How much cost?*, pero al inglés le falta el sujeto y el ayudante: **How much is it?** o **How much does it cost?** Y como «los zapatos» ya suena a varios, se escapa el verbo: ❌ *the shoes is* → ✅ **the shoes are**. Tampoco *the peoples*: **people** ya es plural.

exercises.audio: How much are these shoes?
exercises.tip: shoes es plural, así que va are. Y el precio se pregunta con much, no con many.

accept: How much does this shirt cost?
What does this shirt cost?
exercises.tip: «¿Cuánto cuesta?» = How much is...? Si preguntas con el verbo cost, hace falta does: How much does it cost?

exercises.text: It's twelve dollars and fifty cents.
exercises.tip: Cierra bien las finales: dollars con z, cents con ts. Si las sueltas, suena «dolar» y «cen».
These (estos) y are van con plural: these shoes are.

exercises.audio: They're twenty dollars.
exercises.tip: Escucha bien el número: twenty (20) y twelve (12) empiezan igual.

accept: It's expensive.
That's pricey.
exercises.tip: Hace falta el sujeto: that's (o it's). Y sin a delante del adjetivo solo.

exercises.audio: It's fifty thousand pesos.
accept: It's 50,000 pesos.
exercises.meaning: Son cincuenta mil pesos.
exercises.tip: thousand = mil, y no lleva -s después de un número: fifty thousand, no fifty thousands.

exercises.text: How much ___ they?
exercises.tip: they es plural: are.

exercises.text: She wants cheap shoes.
exercises.tip: She y shoes empiezan con sh suave, como cuando pides silencio. cheap sí es ch, con la t pegada: no las confundas.

exercises.es: Hay muchas personas en la tienda.
exercises.answer: There are a lot of people in the store.
accept: There are many people in the store.
There are lots of people in the store.
There are a lot of people at the store.
There are many people at the store.
There are lots of people at the store.
There are a lot of people in the shop.
There are many people in the shop.
There are lots of people in the shop.
There are a lot of people at the shop.
There are many people at the shop.
There are lots of people at the shop.
exercises.tip: people ya es plural (personas): va con are y nunca lleva -s.
fifteen (15) carga la fuerza al final y alarga la i: fif-TEEN. fifty (50) la carga al principio: FIF-ty.

exercises.es: Los niños están en el parque.
exercises.text: The ___ are in the park.
accept: kids
boys
exercises.tip: child → children. Plural irregular: no se dice childs.

accept: It's twelve dollars and fifty cents.
It costs twelve fifty.
It costs twelve dollars and fifty cents.
It's twelve dollars fifty.
It costs twelve dollars fifty.
It costs $12.50.
exercises.tip: Con precios se usa it's o it costs. «Doce con cincuenta» se dice twelve fifty.

exercises.text: How much is it? It's twelve fifty.
exercises.tip: twelve fifty sale de corrido, como un solo número.

theory.title: like + -ing: el que gusta eres tú
theory.body:
En inglés la persona va primero y el verbo es **like**: *I like coffee.* (Me gusta el café.)

Después de **like, love, hate, enjoy** y **don't mind** (no me molesta) va una cosa o un verbo con **-ing**:
*I **like cooking**.* · *She **loves dancing**.* · *I **don't mind** waiting.*

Con like, love y hate también se oye **to**: *I like to cook.* Con enjoy y don't mind, solo -ing.

Preguntar: ***Do you like** soccer? — Yes, I **do**. / No, I **don't**.*

Y no confundas: **I like** = me gusta (en general). **I'd like** = quisiera (ahora).
theory.trap: «Me gusta» está al revés: no es *It likes me* sino **I like it**. Y lo que sigue va directo: ❌ *I like to the music* · ❌ *I love cook* → ✅ **I like music** · **I love cooking**. El «mucho» va al final: ❌ *I like very much soccer* → ✅ **I like soccer very much**.

exercises.audio: I like cooking.
exercises.tip: Después de like, el verbo va con -ing (cooking) o con to (to cook), pero no los dos.

accept: I love to swim.
exercises.tip: love + -ing. swim dobla la m: swimming.

exercises.text: She hates washing the dishes.
exercises.tip: sh en she, washing y dishes: suave y largo, sin la t de ch.
don't mind = no me molesta. Después va el verbo con -ing.

accept: Do you like to dance?
Do you enjoy dancing?
exercises.tip: Do you like...? pregunta por tus gustos. Would you like to dance? es una invitación: ¿quieres bailar (ahora)?

exercises.audio: Yes, I do. I love it.
options: Yes, I like. I love it.
Yes, I do. I love it.
exercises.answer: Yes, I do. I love it.
exercises.tip: La respuesta corta repite el ayudante: Yes, I do. Y love necesita su objeto: I love it.

exercises.es: Me gusta leer por la noche.
exercises.text: I like ___ at night.
accept: to read
exercises.tip: like + -ing: reading. También vale to read.

exercises.audio: My brother doesn't like shopping.
exercises.meaning: A mi hermano no le gusta ir de compras.
exercises.tip: doesn't se lleva la -s: like queda sin -s. shopping dobla la p.

exercises.text: He hates his job.
exercises.tip: Las tres h suenan: un soplo suave, como cuando empañas un vidrio. No es la j española.

accept: I like soccer very much.
I really like soccer.
I like soccer so much.
I like football a lot.
I like football very much.
I really like football.
I like football so much.
exercises.tip: El «mucho» va al final: I like soccer a lot. En Estados Unidos el fútbol es soccer.

exercises.text: Do you like cooking? — Yes, I ___.
exercises.tip: La respuesta corta usa el ayudante de la pregunta: Do you...? → Yes, I do.

exercises.es: A ella le gusta caminar, pero odia correr.
exercises.answer: She likes walking, but she hates running.
accept: She likes walking but hates running.
She likes to walk, but she hates to run.
She likes to walk but hates to run.
She likes to walk, but she hates running.
She likes to walk but hates running.
She likes walking, but she hates to run.
She likes walking but hates to run.
exercises.tip: Con she, los dos verbos llevan -s: likes, hates. running dobla la n.

exercises.text: Do you like dancing? Yes, I do. I love it.
exercises.tip: Pregunta subiendo al final; la respuesta, bajando.

theory.title: Proponer e invitar
theory.body:
Para proponer algo entre todos: **Let's** + verbo, sin to.
*Let's go to the movies.* · *Let's not wait.*

Para invitar: **Would you like to** + verbo (la más amable) o **Do you want to** + verbo.
*Would you like to come?* · *Do you want to eat something?*

**How about** + una cosa: *How about pizza?* · *How about Friday?* O un verbo con **-ing**, como después de like: *How about going out?*

Aceptar: *Sure!* · *I'd love to.* · *Sounds good.*
Rechazar con cortesía: *Sorry, I can't. I'm busy.*
theory.trap: «Vamos a...» empuja a poner to: ❌ *Let's to go*. Después de **let's** el verbo va pelado: **Let's go**. Con would like pasa lo contrario, sí lleva to: ❌ *Would you like come?* → ✅ **Would you like to come?** Y «¿quieres que vaya?» no se arma con that: ❌ *Do you want that I go?* → ✅ **Do you want me to go?**

exercises.audio: Let's go to the movies.
options: Let's to go to the movies.
exercises.tip: Let's + verbo pelado: let's go. Ir al cine = go to the movies.

options: Would you like come to my house?
Would you like to come to my house?
Do you like to come to my house?
exercises.answer: Would you like to come to my house?
accept: Do you want to come to my house?
Would you like to come over?
Do you want to come over?
Would you like to come to my place?
Would you like to come over to my house?
Do you want to come over to my house?
Do you want to come to my place?
exercises.tip: Would you like + to + verbo. Do you like...? pregunta por gustos, no invita.

exercises.text: Sure! I'd love to.
exercises.tip: La v de love se hace con los dientes de arriba sobre el labio de abajo. No la cambies por b.

accept: Today, let's not go.
exercises.tip: Para negar una propuesta: let's not + verbo.

exercises.es: Lo siento, no puedo. Estoy ocupado.
options: Sorry, I don't can. I'm busy.
Sorry, I can't. I have busy.
accept: I'm sorry, I can't. I'm busy.
Sorry, I can't make it. I'm busy.
I'm sorry, I can't make it. I'm busy.
exercises.tip: Ocupado es un estado: I'm busy (con be), no I have busy.

exercises.text: Do you want ___ eat something?
exercises.tip: want pide to antes del verbo: want to eat.

exercises.audio: How about Friday night?
exercises.tip: How about + una cosa o un día, sin to: How about Friday night?

exercises.audio: Sounds good. See you at eight.
accept: Sounds good. See you at 8:00.
exercises.meaning: Me parece bien. Nos vemos a las ocho.
exercises.tip: Sounds good = me parece bien. Es una forma corta de aceptar.

exercises.text: How about this Thursday?
exercises.tip: this y Thursday llevan th: la punta de la lengua asoma entre los dientes. En this vibra; en Thursday es solo aire.

accept: Let's have pizza tonight.
Let's get pizza tonight.
Let's eat some pizza tonight.
Let's have some pizza tonight.
Let's get some pizza tonight.
Tonight let's eat pizza.
Let's eat pizza this evening.
Let's have pizza this evening.
Tonight let's have pizza.
Tonight let's get pizza.
exercises.tip: «Comamos» es una propuesta: let's + verbo.

exercises.text: Would you like to dance? — I'd ___ to!
exercises.tip: I'd love to = me encantaría. El to del final reemplaza al verbo: no hace falta repetir dance.

exercises.answer: Do you want to come with us?
accept: Would you like to come with us?
Want to come with us?
Do you want to join us?
Would you like to join us?
Do you want to go with us?
Would you like to go with us?
Do you want to come along with us?
Would you like to come along with us?
exercises.tip: Do you want + to + verbo. Con would you like suena más amable.

exercises.text: Let's go to the movies. Sure, sounds good!
exercises.tip: Let's go sale como una sola palabra: «letsgou».

units.title: Lo que pasó
units.subtitle: Was/were, la -ed, irregulares y did

theory.title: was y were: el pasado de to be
theory.body:
El pasado de **am/is/are** son solo dos palabras:

**was** → I, he, she, it
*I **was** tired.* · *She **was** at home.*

**were** → you, we, they
*You **were** right.* · *They **were** happy.*

**Negativo:** wasn't / weren't
**Pregunta:** *Were you at the party?* · *Was he there?*

**Respuesta corta:** *Were you tired?* → *Yes, I **was**.* · *No, I **wasn't**.*
theory.trap: «Estuve en la fiesta» sale como *I was in the party* — y eso significa que estabas *dentro* del concepto fiesta. Para eventos el inglés usa **at**: **I was at the party**. Lo mismo con at school, at work, at the concert.

exercises.tip: Eventos con at: at the party, at the concert. Y también at work, at school.
they siempre con were.

exercises.audio: She was at home yesterday.
exercises.tip: she → was. Estar en casa: at home (en EE. UU. también She was home). Con go, sin at: go home.

exercises.audio: We weren't ready.
exercises.tip: we → were → weren't.
you → were, y at work sin the.

exercises.audio: It was a good day.
exercises.meaning: Fue un buen día.
exercises.tip: it → was, y a good day con artículo.

exercises.text: I was at home last night.
exercises.tip: home con h soplada.

exercises.text: They were at the coffee shop.
exercises.tip: shop con sh de «shhh», no «chop».

exercises.text: I was ___ the party.
exercises.tip: Eventos con at: at the party, at work, at school. in sería dentro.

accept: Yesterday they were tired.
exercises.tip: they siempre con were, nunca was.

exercises.text: I was at home last night.
exercises.tip: Seis palabras de un tirón. El peso en «HOME» y en «NIGHT».

exercises.text: Were you at home? Yes, I ___.
accept: was at home
was home
exercises.tip: Te preguntan con you (were), pero respondes con I: Yes, I was.

accept: No, he wasn't tired.
exercises.tip: Pregunta con Was → respuesta corta con was: No, he wasn't. weren't es para you, we, they, e isn't es presente.

exercises.answer: Was she at the office yesterday?
accept: Was she in the office yesterday?
exercises.tip: Para preguntar en pasado, Was va antes del sujeto: Was she…?

exercises.audio: Were they at the party?
exercises.tip: they va con were, y en la pregunta were va primero.

theory.title: La -ed, y cómo suena de verdad
theory.body:
Para el pasado de la mayoría de verbos se pega **-ed** al final:

*work → work**ed*** · *play → play**ed*** · *live → live**d***

Ortografía: consonante + y cambia a **-ied** (*study → stud**ied***), y algunos cortos doblan la última letra (*stop → sto**pped***).

Y no cambia con la persona: **I worked, he worked, they worked**. Una sola forma para todos.

Lo difícil no es escribirla: es **sonarla**. La -ed suena de tres maneras y casi nunca es una sílaba nueva:

- **/t/** tras sonido sordo: *walked* suena «wokt», *asked* suena «askt»
- **/d/** tras sonido sonoro: *played* suena «pleid», *lived* suena «livd»
- **/id/** — sílaba de verdad — **solo** tras t o d: *wanted* «wonted», *needed* «nidid»
theory.trap: El error insignia: decir *walk-ed* como dos sílabas, «wok-ed». En español todas las letras suenan, así que la mano y la boca quieren pronunciar esa e. En inglés la e es muda salvo tras t o d. Son **walked** «wokt», **talked** «tokt», **asked** «askt» — una sola sílaba. Y en *walk* y *talk* la l tampoco suena.

accept: Yesterday I worked.
exercises.tip: yesterday pide pasado: worked.
live ya termina en e, así que solo se le suma d.

exercises.audio: They played at home.
exercises.tip: played suena «pleid», en una sola sílaba; antes de vocal la d se oye bien.

exercises.audio: I wanted to call you.
exercises.tip: Aquí sí es sílaba aparte: want termina en t, así que wanted suena «WON-ted».
study cambia la y: studied. Y «el año pasado» es last year, sin the.

exercises.audio: She asked me a question.
exercises.meaning: Ella me hizo una pregunta.
exercises.tip: asked se escribe con -ed aunque suene «askt».

exercises.text: I walked to work yesterday.
exercises.tip: walked es UNA sílaba: «wokt». Si dices «wok-ed» te lo va a marcar.

exercises.text: She asked and I answered.
exercises.tip: asked «askt», answered «AN-serd». Ninguna de las dos gana una sílaba.

exercises.text: Yesterday I ___ to work.
exercises.tip: walked se escribe con -ed pero suena «wokt», en una sola sílaba.

exercises.es: Mis padres vivieron en Cali el año pasado.
exercises.answer: My parents lived in Cali last year.
accept: Last year my parents lived in Cali.
exercises.tip: live ya termina en e: solo se suma d. Y «el año pasado» es last year, sin the.

exercises.text: She asked me a question.
exercises.tip: asked es «askt», una sílaba. Si suena «ask-ed» se te alarga la frase entera.
Las dos terminan en «t». Lo que cambia es la vocal: wor- lleva r.

theory.title: Los irregulares: hay que aprendérselos
theory.body:
Unos 100 verbos no siguen la regla de -ed. Y son justo los que más se usan. No hay truco: se memorizan.

Los diez que más vas a necesitar:

| ahora | pasado | |
|---|---|---|
| go | **went** | ir |
| have | **had** | tener |
| do | **did** | hacer |
| say | **said** | decir |
| see | **saw** | ver |
| get | **got** | conseguir |
| make | **made** | hacer |
| come | **came** | venir |
| take | **took** | tomar |
| eat | **ate** | comer |

Y como los regulares: **no cambian con la persona**. I went, he went, they went. El único que cambia es **be**: *was / were*.
theory.trap: El error no suele ser el verbo suelto, sino mezclarlo: *I didn't went* ❌. Cuando aparece **did** o **didn't**, el verbo vuelve a su forma normal: **I didn't go**. El did ya carga el pasado, igual que el does cargaba la -s.

options: I goed to the doctor yesterday.
I went to the doctor yesterday.
I was go to the doctor yesterday.
exercises.answer: I went to the doctor yesterday.
accept: Yesterday I went to the doctor.
I went to see the doctor yesterday.
exercises.tip: go → went. No existe goed.

accept: She had an issue.
exercises.tip: have → had, para todas las personas.

exercises.audio: We saw a good movie.
exercises.tip: see → saw. seen es otra forma, todavía no la necesitas.

exercises.audio: He made dinner last night.
exercises.tip: make → made. Y la comida se make, no se do.
come → came.

exercises.audio: I took the bus to work.
exercises.meaning: Tomé el bus al trabajo.
exercises.tip: take → took.

exercises.text: I went home early.
exercises.tip: home con la h soplada.

exercises.text: She said three things.
exercises.tip: three y things con la lengua entre los dientes. Y said suena «sed», no «seid».

exercises.text: I ___ to the doctor yesterday.
exercises.tip: go se vuelve went. No existe goed.

exercises.es: Ella tuvo un problema con su carro.
exercises.answer: She had a problem with her car.
accept: She had a problem with the car.
She had a problem with his car.
She had a problem with their car.
She had a problem with your car.
She had trouble with her car.
She had an issue with her car.
She had trouble with the car.
She had an issue with the car.
exercises.tip: have se vuelve had, para todas las personas.

exercises.text: I took the bus to work.
exercises.tip: Frase corta y muy usada. «I TOOK the bus to WORK».

exercises.text: I ___ chicken for lunch.
accept: had
exercises.tip: El pasado de eat es ate (suena «éit»), no «eated».

accept: She found a new job.
She landed a new job.
exercises.tip: El pasado de get (conseguir) es got.

options: I did my homework last night.
I doed my homework last night.
I made my homework last night.
exercises.answer: I did my homework last night.
accept: I did the homework last night.
Last night I did my homework.
Last night I did the homework.
exercises.tip: La tarea se hace con do (did), no con make: «hacer» se traduce de dos formas.

theory.title: did y didn't
theory.body:
Para negar y preguntar en pasado hay un solo ayudante, y sirve para todos: **did**.

**Negar:** didn't + verbo normal
*I **didn't go**.* · *She **didn't work**.*

**Preguntar:** Did + sujeto + verbo normal
***Did** you **go**?* · ***Did** he **call**?*

La regla es la misma de siempre, con otra cara: **cuando aparece did, el verbo vuelve a su forma base**. El pasado ya está en el did.

*I didn't went* ❌ → *I didn't **go*** ✅
*Did you went?* ❌ → *Did you **go**?* ✅

Excepción: con **was/were** no se usa did: *I **wasn't** tired* · ***Were** you there?*
theory.trap: Poner el pasado dos veces es el error más común de todos, y no es tontería: en español «no fui» lleva el pasado en el verbo, porque no hay ayudante. En inglés el pasado lo carga el did y el verbo se queda desnudo. Si ves did o didn't en tu frase, revisa que el verbo esté en su forma base: go (no went), work (no worked), sin -s.

options: I didn't went to the party.
I didn't go to the party.
I not went to the party.
exercises.answer: I didn't go to the party.
exercises.tip: didn't ya es el pasado: go va en su forma base.

accept: Did you talk to her?
Did you speak to her?
Did you talk with her?
exercises.tip: Did + speak, no spoke.

exercises.audio: She didn't visit us.
exercises.tip: didn't + visit, sin -ed.

exercises.audio: Did they want more food?
exercises.tip: Después de did, siempre la forma base.
didn't + see. El saw no va porque el did ya carga el pasado.

exercises.audio: Did you have a good weekend?
exercises.meaning: ¿Tuviste un buen fin de semana?
exercises.tip: Did + have, no had. Pregunta de lunes por la mañana.

exercises.text: I didn't have time.
exercises.tip: have con la h soplada.

exercises.text: Did you watch the show?
exercises.tip: show con sh. Y watch termina en ch, que es distinto.

exercises.text: I didn't ___ to the party.
exercises.tip: didn't ya carga el pasado: el verbo vuelve a su forma normal.

exercises.answer: Did you speak with her yesterday?
accept: Did you talk to her yesterday?
Did you speak to her yesterday?
Did you talk with her yesterday?
exercises.tip: Did + speak, no spoke. El pasado ya está en el did.

exercises.text: Did you have a good weekend?
exercises.tip: La pregunta del lunes. Suena «did-ya HAVE a good WEEKend?».

units.title: Preguntar por el pasado
units.subtitle: Where did you go?, había y respuestas cortas

theory.title: Where did you go? y «había»
theory.body:
Para preguntar en pasado con **where, what, when, who**: palabra de pregunta + **did** + sujeto + verbo **normal**.
*Where **did** you **go**?* · *When **did** she **arrive**?* (Si **who** es quien hizo la acción, va sin did: *Who called?*)

Respuestas cortas: *Yes, I **did**.* · *No, he **didn't**.* Con be: *Yes, it **was**.*

**Había** (cuando significa «existía») es el pasado de *there is / there are*:
**there was** + una cosa (o algo que no se cuenta: *a lot of noise*) · **there were** + varias
*There **was** a party.* · *There **were** many people.*
Pregunta: ***Was there** a problem?* · ***Were there** many people?*
theory.trap: En español basta la entonación, y sale *Where you went?*; o, mezclando, *Where did you went?* Con **did** el verbo vuelve a su forma normal: **Where did you go?** Y el «había» de existir no es *had* ni *there had*: ❌ *Had a party* → ✅ **There was a party**. Con gente va were: ❌ *There was many people* → ✅ **There were many people**.

exercises.audio: Where did you go?
exercises.tip: El pasado ya está en did: el verbo queda en go, no en went.

options: What you did on the weekend?
What did you do on the weekend?
What did you did on the weekend?
exercises.answer: What did you do on the weekend?
accept: What did you do over the weekend?
What did you do this weekend?
What did you do last weekend?
What did you do this past weekend?
What did you do at the weekend?
exercises.tip: What + did + you + do: el primer do es el ayudante (did), el segundo es el verbo hacer.

exercises.text: There were a lot of people there.
exercises.tip: There lleva th que vibra: lengua entre los dientes, no una d.
Con did, arrive sin -ed. Y llegó es pasado: did, no does.

exercises.audio: There were many people.
exercises.tip: people es plural: there were. «Había» nunca se dice con had.

accept: Was there an issue?
Was there any problem?
exercises.tip: Para preguntar se voltea: there was → was there?

exercises.text: Who ___ you see at the party?
exercises.tip: Aquí who es a quien viste (tú viste): hace falta did y see queda normal.

exercises.audio: No, she didn't. She stayed home.
exercises.meaning: No, ella no. Se quedó en casa.
exercises.tip: Respuesta corta: No, she didn't, sin repetir el verbo.

exercises.text: What did you do last weekend?
exercises.tip: Cierra las finales: la d de did, la st de last, la d de weekend.
Where + did + you + go. Nada de went después de did.

exercises.text: Was the movie good? — Yes, it ___.
exercises.tip: Si la pregunta va con was, la respuesta corta también: Yes, it was.

exercises.answer: Were there a lot of people at the concert?
accept: Were there many people at the concert?
Were there lots of people at the concert?
Was the concert crowded?
Was it crowded at the concert?
Was there a big crowd at the concert?
exercises.tip: gente = people, que es plural: were there, no was there.

exercises.text: Where did you go? Was there a party?
exercises.tip: La pregunta con where baja al final; la de sí o no (Was there...?) sube.

units.title: Lo que viene
units.subtitle: Going to, will y comparar

theory.title: be going to: planes que ya están decididos
theory.body:
Para lo que ya tienes planeado:

**am / is / are + going to + verbo**

*I **am going to** travel next week.*
*She **is going to** study medicine.*
*They **are going to** move to Cali.*

Se parece mucho al español «voy a viajar», y por una vez la traducción funciona pieza por pieza. Lo único que no se puede olvidar es el **am/is/are** del principio.

Al hablar rápido, *going to* suena «gonna». Lo vas a oír muchísimo, pero solo antes de un verbo: *I'm gonna travel*, y nunca *I'm gonna Cali* (eso es *I'm going to Cali*).
theory.trap: El calco directo es *I go to travel* — porque en español «voy» ya es el verbo ir. En inglés hacen falta las tres piezas: **I am going to travel**. Si te falta el am/is/are, la frase se rompe.

exercises.es: Voy a viajar la próxima semana.
options: I go to travel next week.
I am going to travel next week.
I going to travel next week.
exercises.answer: I am going to travel next week.
accept: I'm traveling next week.
Next week I am going to travel.
I will travel next week.
I'm gonna travel next week.
exercises.tip: Las tres piezas: am + going to + verbo.

exercises.es: Ella va a estudiar medicina el próximo año.
options: She is going to study medicine next year.
She go to study medicine next year.
She is going study medicine next year.
exercises.answer: She is going to study medicine next year.
accept: Next year she is going to study medicine.
She will study medicine next year.
She's gonna study medicine next year.
exercises.tip: going to nunca pierde su to.

exercises.audio: We are going to buy a house.
options: We going to buy a house.
We are going to buy a house.
We are going to buying a house.
exercises.answer: We are going to buy a house.
exercises.tip: Después de to, el verbo va desnudo: buy.

exercises.audio: He isn't going to come.
exercises.tip: Se niega el is: isn't going to.

exercises.answer: What are you going to do tomorrow?
exercises.tip: What + are you + going to + do.

exercises.audio: I am going to call you later.
exercises.meaning: Te voy a llamar más tarde.
exercises.tip: call you, sin to en medio.

exercises.text: I am going to study tonight.
exercises.tip: study sin e delante.

exercises.text: She is going to help me.
exercises.tip: help con la h soplada.

exercises.es: Voy a viajar la próxima semana.
exercises.text: I am ___ to travel next week.
exercises.tip: Las tres piezas: am + going + to. Si falta alguna, la frase se rompe.

exercises.es: ¿Qué vas a hacer el fin de semana?
exercises.answer: What are you going to do this weekend?
accept: What are you gonna do this weekend?
What will you do this weekend?
What are you doing this weekend?
What are you going to do on the weekend?
What are you gonna do on the weekend?
What will you do on the weekend?
What are you doing on the weekend?
What are you going to do over the weekend?
What are you gonna do over the weekend?
What will you do over the weekend?
What are you doing over the weekend?
What are you going to do for the weekend?
What are you doing for the weekend?
exercises.tip: Con going to es lo ya planeado. What are you doing...? también sirve para planes.

exercises.text: I am going to study tonight.
exercises.tip: Di «going to» completo. El peso cae en «STU-dy» y en «to-NIGHT».

theory.title: will: lo que decides en el momento
theory.body:
**will** es para lo que **no** tenías planeado: una decisión que tomas ahora mismo, una promesa, una predicción.

*The phone is ringing. I'**ll** get it.* (lo decides en ese segundo)
*I think it **will** rain.* (predicción)
*I **won't** forget.* (promesa)

Como **can**, no cambia nunca: I will, he will, they will. Y lo que sigue va desnudo, sin to.

**will not = won't**

La diferencia con *going to*: **going to** ya estaba decidido, **will** se decide al hablar.

**Pregunta:** will va delante: ***Will** you help me?* · ***Will** it rain tomorrow?*
theory.trap: En español el futuro va pegado al verbo («lloverá», «iré»), así que no hay una palabra suelta que recordar y se olvida el will. Y ojo: *I will to go* ❌ — igual que can, will no lleva to: **I will go**.

options: I think it will to rain.
accept: I think that it will rain.
I think it is going to rain.
exercises.tip: will + verbo desnudo, sin to y sin -s.

accept: I won't forget it.
I won't forget that.
exercises.tip: won't es will not. Se escribe raro pero es de las más usadas.

exercises.audio: I'll help you.
exercises.tip: I'll es I will. Al hablar casi siempre se contrae.

exercises.audio: She will be here soon.
exercises.tip: Después de will va be, no is.
will + call, sin to.

exercises.audio: It won't be easy.
exercises.meaning: No será fácil.
exercises.tip: won't se escribe w-o-n-apóstrofo-t.

exercises.text: I think it will be hot.
exercises.tip: think con la lengua entre los dientes. No es «tink».

exercises.text: I will help you with this.
exercises.tip: help con h soplada, y this con th.

exercises.text: Are you cold? I ___ close the window.
accept: 'll
exercises.tip: Lo decides en este segundo: will (I'll close it), no going to.

accept: I won't forget it.
I won't forget that.
I'm not going to forget.
I'm not going to forget it.
exercises.tip: won't es will not. Se escribe raro pero se usa muchísimo.

exercises.text: I think it will be hot.
exercises.tip: think con la lengua entre los dientes, y sin parar antes de «hot».
won't es larga, como «wount»; want es corta. Cambian la frase entera.

accept: Are you going to help me?
exercises.tip: Para preguntar, will va antes del sujeto: Will you…? El verbo sigue sin to.

exercises.text: ___ you come to the party?
exercises.tip: Pregunta en futuro: Will you come…? No lleva do.

options: Will you be at home tomorrow?
Will you are at home tomorrow?
Do you will be at home tomorrow?
exercises.answer: Will you be at home tomorrow?
accept: Will you be home tomorrow?
Are you going to be at home tomorrow?
Are you going to be home tomorrow?
exercises.tip: Después de will, to be se queda como be: Will you be…?

theory.title: Comparar: -er o more, nunca los dos
theory.body:
La regla depende del **largo** del adjetivo.

**Cortos (una sílaba)** → **-er ... than**
*bigger than* · *older than* · *cheaper than*
Si termina en **una sola** vocal + una consonante, la consonante se dobla: *big → bi**gg**er*, *hot → ho**tt**er*. Con dos vocales no se dobla (*cheap → cheaper*), y la w nunca (*new → newer*).

**Dos sílabas terminadas en -y** → **-ier**: *easy → eas**ier***

**Largos (dos sílabas o más)** → **more ... than**
*more expensive than* · *more interesting than*

Y para el máximo, lo mismo con **the**:
*the big**gest*** · *the **most** expensive*

Tres que se salen de todo y hay que memorizar:
*good → **better** → the **best***
*bad → **worse** → the **worst***
*far → **farther** → the **farthest*** (también *further*)
theory.trap: *more big* ❌ es calco de «más grande», y suena mal de inmediato a un oído inglés. Los cortos llevan **-er**: **bigger**. Y nunca los dos juntos: *more bigger* ❌. El otro: comparar es con **than**, no con *that* — se parecen demasiado al escribir.

exercises.es: Mi carro es más grande que el tuyo.
options: My car is more big than yours.
My car is bigger than yours.
My car is bigger that yours.
exercises.answer: My car is bigger than yours.
accept: My car is larger than yours.
exercises.tip: big es corto: bigger. Y se compara con than.

accept: This hotel costs more.
exercises.tip: expensive es largo: lleva more.

exercises.audio: She is older than me.
options: She is more old than me.
exercises.tip: old → older.

exercises.audio: This is the best restaurant here.
options: This is the most good restaurant here.
This is the best restaurant here.
This is the better restaurant here.
exercises.answer: This is the best restaurant here.
exercises.tip: good → better → the best. Irregular, de memoria.

exercises.es: Hoy está más frío que ayer.
exercises.tip: cold es corto: colder than.

exercises.audio: My English is better now.
exercises.meaning: Mi inglés está mejor ahora.
exercises.tip: better, no more good.

exercises.text: This is better than that.
exercises.tip: Tres th: this, than, that. Lengua entre los dientes en las tres.

exercises.text: This shirt is cheaper.
exercises.tip: shirt con sh. cheaper empieza con ch, que es otro sonido.

exercises.es: Mi carro es más grande que el tuyo.
exercises.text: My car is ___ than yours.
accept: larger
exercises.tip: big es corto: bigger (se dobla la g, como hot → hotter). Nada de more big.

exercises.es: Este hotel es más caro que el otro.
exercises.answer: This hotel is more expensive than the other one.
accept: This hotel is more expensive than the other.
This hotel is more expensive than the other hotel.
This hotel costs more than the other one.
exercises.tip: expensive es largo: lleva more. Y se compara con than, no con that.

exercises.text: This is better than that.
exercises.tip: Tres th en la misma frase: this, than, that. Despacio la primera vez.
cheap empieza con ch; sheep con sh. Es el par que más se nos mezcla.

exercises.es: Esta es la ciudad más grande de Colombia.
exercises.answer: This is the biggest city in Colombia.
accept: This is the largest city in Colombia.
This is Colombia's biggest city.
This is Colombia's largest city.
exercises.tip: El máximo: the + -est (biggest, con la g doblada). Y «de Colombia» aquí es in Colombia, no of.

exercises.es: El inglés es más fácil que el francés.
exercises.text: English is ___ than French.
exercises.tip: easy termina en -y: la y cambia a i y se pone -er, easier. No «more easy».

exercises.es: Hoy es el peor día de mi vida.
exercises.text: Today is the ___ day of my life.
exercises.tip: bad → worse → the worst. Es irregular: nada de «baddest».

exercises.es: Mi inglés es peor que el tuyo.
options: My English is more bad than yours.
My English is worse than yours.
My English is badder than yours.
exercises.answer: My English is worse than yours.
exercises.tip: «Peor que» es worse than. bad no sigue la regla.

levels.title: Defenderte de verdad
levels.goal: Contar lo que pasó, hablar de planes, dar consejo y opinar sin quedarte trabado.

units.title: Lo que estabas haciendo
units.subtitle: El pasado que seguía pasando: was doing y used to

theory.title: Dos pasados en la misma frase
theory.body:
El inglés usa dos pasados a la vez para contar qué pasó mientras pasaba otra cosa.

**Pasado continuo** (was/were + -ing) = el fondo, lo que ya venía pasando.
**Pasado simple** = lo que ocurrió de golpe y lo interrumpió.

*It **was raining** when I **went** out.*
*I **was sleeping** when she **called**.*

Dos palabras que los amarran:
**when** + pasado simple (el golpe): *when she called*
**while** + pasado continuo (el fondo): *while I was sleeping*

Ojo: **when** también puede llevar el fondo: *When I was walking home, I saw Ana.* Lo que no cambia es que el fondo va en continuo.
theory.trap: En español decimos «llovía» y «estaba lloviendo» casi igual, así que sale *It rained when I went out* — que significa otra cosa: que empezó a llover justo cuando saliste. Si algo ya venía pasando, va **was/were + -ing**.

exercises.audio: I was sleeping when she called.
options: I was sleeping when she called.
I was sleep when she called.
exercises.answer: I was sleeping when she called.
exercises.tip: was + sleeping: era el fondo. La llamada lo interrumpió.

options: It rained when I went out.
It was raining when I went out.
It was rain when I went out.
exercises.answer: It was raining when I went out.
accept: It was raining when I left.
It was raining when I left the house.
It was raining when I went outside.
exercises.tip: La lluvia ya venía: pasado continuo.

exercises.text: They ___ working when I arrived.
exercises.tip: they lleva were, nunca was.

exercises.answer: What were you doing at eight?
accept: What were you doing at eight o'clock?
What were you doing at 8:00?
exercises.tip: were + you + doing. Y las horas con at.

exercises.es: Mientras yo cocinaba, él leía el periódico.
exercises.answer: While I was cooking, he was reading the newspaper.
accept: While I was cooking, he read the newspaper.
He was reading the newspaper while I was cooking.
He read the newspaper while I was cooking.
While I was cooking, he was reading the paper.
He was reading the paper while I was cooking.
While I was cooking, he read the paper.
exercises.tip: while va con el continuo. Los dos en continuo si los dos son fondo; el segundo también vale en pasado simple.
Se niega el was: was not, o wasn't.

exercises.audio: We were waiting for the bus.
exercises.meaning: Estábamos esperando el bus.
exercises.tip: Esperar A algo o a alguien es wait for: wait for the bus.

exercises.text: I was working when you called.
exercises.tip: called suena «kold», una sola sílaba. Nada de «kol-ed».

exercises.text: It was raining when I went out.
exercises.tip: Dos bloques: «it was RAINing» / «when I went OUT». Respira solo en el medio.

theory.title: used to: lo que hacías y ya no
theory.body:
Para hábitos y estados del pasado que **ya no son**:

**used to** + verbo
*I **used to** smoke.* (fumaba, ya no)
*She **used to** live in Cali.* (vivía, ya no)

Negativo y pregunta pierden la **d**, porque aparece el did:
*I **didn't use to** like coffee.*
***Did** you **use to** play soccer?*

Y no sirve para algo que pasó una sola vez: *I used to go to Spain in 2019* ❌ → *I went to Spain in 2019* ✅

No confundir con **be used to** + sustantivo o -ing = *estar acostumbrado*: *I'm **used to** the cold.* · *She isn't **used to** driving at night.*
theory.trap: El español lo dice con el imperfecto —«fumaba», «vivía»—, la misma forma que usamos para el fondo de una escena. Por eso sale *I was smoking* cuando quieres decir «antes fumaba». Si es un hábito que se acabó, es **used to**.

accept: I used to be a smoker.
exercises.tip: Hábito que se acabó: used to + verbo pelado.

exercises.audio: She used to live in Cali.
options: She used to live in Cali.
exercises.answer: She used to live in Cali.
exercises.tip: Después de used to, el verbo va sin cambios.

exercises.es: Antes no me gustaba el café.
exercises.text: I didn't ___ to like coffee.
exercises.tip: Con did, se cae la d: use to, no used to.

exercises.answer: Did you use to play soccer?
accept: Did you use to play football?
exercises.tip: Did + use to + verbo. La d se pierde por el did.

exercises.es: Mi papá trabajaba en un banco.
exercises.answer: My father used to work in a bank.
accept: My dad used to work in a bank.
My father used to work at a bank.
My dad used to work at a bank.
My dad worked at a bank.
My dad worked in a bank.
My father worked at a bank.
My father worked in a bank.
My dad used to work for a bank.
My father used to work for a bank.
My dad worked for a bank.
My father worked for a bank.
exercises.tip: Un trabajo de antes que ya no tiene: used to.

exercises.answer: They didn't use to live here.
exercises.tip: didn't + use to + live.

exercises.audio: I used to walk to school.
exercises.meaning: Antes caminaba a la escuela.
exercises.tip: used to se escribe con d cuando no hay did.

exercises.text: I used to live in a small house.
exercises.tip: house con la h soplada. Y used to suena «YUUS-tu», pegado.

exercises.text: She used to work here.
exercises.tip: «used to» va pegado, casi una palabra: «YUUS-tu». El peso en WORK.

exercises.answer: I'm used to getting up early.
accept: I'm used to waking up early.
I'm accustomed to getting up early.
I'm accustomed to waking up early.
I'm used to getting up early in the morning.
I'm used to waking up early in the morning.
I'm used to early mornings.
I have gotten used to getting up early.
I have gotten used to waking up early.
exercises.tip: be used to + -ing = estar acostumbrado a. No es lo mismo que used to + verbo (antes hacía).

options: I used to the cold now.
I'm used to the cold now.
I used to be cold now.
exercises.answer: I'm used to the cold now.
accept: I'm already used to the cold.
I'm used to the cold already.
I'm used to the cold.
I have gotten used to the cold.
I have gotten used to the cold now.
I got used to the cold.
I'm accustomed to the cold now.
I am now used to the cold.
I have already gotten used to the cold.
exercises.tip: Con be delante (I'm used to) es «estar acostumbrado»; sin be (I used to) es «antes hacía».

exercises.es: Ella no está acostumbrada a manejar de noche.
exercises.text: She isn't used to ___ at night.
exercises.tip: En be used to, el to va seguido de sustantivo o de -ing: used to driving.

theory.title: Amarrar una historia: when, while, so, because
theory.body:
Para contar algo no basta con los verbos: hacen falta las palabras que unen.

**when** = cuando (el golpe) · **while** = mientras (el fondo)
**so** = así que (consecuencia) · **because** = porque (causa)
**then** = entonces, después · **suddenly** = de repente

*I was walking home **when** it started to rain, **so** I took a taxi.*

Fíjate en el orden: **so** va delante de lo que pasó *después*; **because** delante de la *razón*. En español «así que» y «porque» funcionan igual, pero se confunden al traducir rápido.
theory.trap: En español se dice «**Como** llovía, **por eso** tomé un taxi», con dos piezas. En inglés **nunca se ponen because y so juntos**: *Because it was raining, so I took a taxi* ❌. O *Because it was raining, I took a taxi*, o *It was raining, so I took a taxi* — una de las dos, no las dos.

exercises.es: Estaba caminando a casa cuando empezó a llover.
options: I walked home when it started to rain.
I was walking home when it started to rain.
I was walking home while it started to rain.
exercises.answer: I was walking home when it started to rain.
accept: I was walking home when it started raining.
I was walking home when it began to rain.
I was walking home when it began raining.
exercises.tip: El fondo en continuo; el golpe con when + pasado simple.

exercises.audio: It was late, so we went home.
options: It was late, because we went home.
It was late, so we went home.
It was late, so we go home.
exercises.answer: It was late, so we went home.
exercises.tip: so introduce la consecuencia.

exercises.text: I didn't go out ___ it was raining.
accept: since
as
exercises.tip: because introduce la razón.

exercises.answer: While I was waiting, I read the newspaper.
accept: I read the newspaper while I was waiting.
While I waited, I read the newspaper.
I read the newspaper while I waited.
While I was waiting, I read the paper.
I read the paper while I was waiting.
exercises.tip: while con el continuo. Y el pasado de read se escribe igual pero suena «red».

exercises.es: De repente alguien tocó la puerta.
exercises.answer: Suddenly someone knocked on the door.
accept: Someone suddenly knocked on the door.
Suddenly somebody knocked on the door.
Somebody suddenly knocked on the door.
Suddenly someone knocked at the door.
Someone suddenly knocked at the door.
Suddenly somebody knocked at the door.
All of a sudden someone knocked on the door.
exercises.tip: knock on (o at) the door. La k inicial no suena.

exercises.es: Perdí el bus, así que llegué tarde.
exercises.answer: I missed the bus, so I was late.
exercises.tip: «Perder el bus» es miss, no lose. Y llegar tarde es be late.

exercises.audio: Then she opened the window.
exercises.meaning: Entonces ella abrió la ventana.
exercises.tip: opened suena «OU-pend», dos sílabas, no tres.

exercises.text: I missed the bus, so I walked.
exercises.tip: missed «mist» y walked «wokt». Las dos de una sílaba.

exercises.text: Suddenly someone knocked on the door.
exercises.tip: La k de knock no suena: «NOKT». El peso en SUD-denly y en DOOR.

units.title: Lo que ya hiciste
units.subtitle: El present perfect, y cuándo NO usarlo

theory.title: have + participio
theory.body:
El present perfect se arma con dos piezas:

**have / has** + **participio** (la tercera forma del verbo)

*I **have finished**.* · *She **has gone**.*

El participio de los regulares es igual al pasado (worked, lived). Los irregulares hay que aprenderlos:
*go → went → **gone*** · *see → saw → **seen*** · *do → did → **done***
*eat → ate → **eaten*** · *write → wrote → **written***

Se usa para algo del pasado **que todavía importa ahora**: no dices cuándo pasó, dices que ya está.

Las **respuestas cortas** repiten el ayudante: *Have you finished?* → ***Yes, I have.*** / ***No, I haven't.*** Es más natural que contestar con el verbo (*Yes, I finished*).
theory.trap: Cuidado con **has**, no **have**, para he/she/it — es la misma -s de siempre, escondida. *She have finished* ❌ → *She **has** finished* ✅

accept: I have already finished.
I have finished already.
I already finished.
I am done.
exercises.tip: have + participio. finished es regular.

exercises.audio: She has gone home.
exercises.tip: she lleva has. Y el participio de go es gone, no went.

exercises.text: He ___ seen that movie.
exercises.tip: he lleva has.

accept: I still haven't eaten.
I have not yet eaten.
I didn't eat yet.
exercises.tip: El participio de eat es eaten. Y «todavía» en negativo es yet, al final.

accept: They have finished the work.
They have done the job.
They have finished the job.
exercises.tip: El participio de do es done.
El participio de write es written.

exercises.audio: I have lost my keys.
exercises.meaning: He perdido mis llaves.
exercises.tip: lose → lost → lost. Aquí importa que siguen perdidas.

exercises.text: I have finished the homework.
exercises.tip: have y homework: las dos h se soplan.

exercises.text: She has gone to the store.
exercises.tip: «has gone» se pega: «shiz-GON». El peso en GONE y en STORE.

accept: Have you finished yet?
Have you already finished?
Have you finished already?
Are you done?
Are you done yet?
Are you finished?
Are you finished yet?
Did you finish?
Did you finish yet?
Did you already finish?
Are you already done?
Are you done already?
Did you finish already?
exercises.tip: Pregunta: have va antes del sujeto y el participio después.

exercises.text: Has she finished? Yes, she ___.
exercises.tip: La respuesta corta repite el ayudante: Yes, she has / No, she hasn't.

exercises.audio: No, I haven't.
exercises.tip: A una pregunta con have se contesta con have: No, I haven't.

theory.title: Experiencias: ever, never, been y gone
theory.body:
El present perfect es el tiempo de las **experiencias de vida**, sin decir cuándo.

***Have you ever** been to Mexico?* (¿alguna vez?)
*I'**ve never** eaten sushi.* (nunca, hasta hoy)

Y hay una pareja que confunde a todo el mundo:

**been** = fue y **ya volvió**
*She has **been** to Paris.* (la conoce, está aquí)

**gone** = fue y **sigue allá**
*She has **gone** to Paris.* (no está, se fue)
theory.trap: *Have you ever went...?* ❌ es el error más común: se mete el pasado simple donde va el participio. Con have siempre va la tercera forma: **Have you ever been...?**

options: Have you ever went to Mexico?
Have you ever been to Mexico?
Did you ever been to Mexico?
exercises.answer: Have you ever been to Mexico?
accept: Have you ever been in Mexico?
Have you ever visited Mexico?
Did you ever go to Mexico?
exercises.tip: Con have va been, no went.

exercises.audio: I have never eaten sushi.
exercises.tip: never va entre have y el participio.

exercises.es: Ella se fue a París y todavía está allá.
exercises.text: She has ___ to Paris.
exercises.tip: Sigue allá: gone. Si ya hubiera vuelto sería been.

accept: I have never seen the snow.
exercises.tip: El participio de see es seen.

exercises.answer: Have you ever worked at night?
accept: Have you ever worked nights?
Have you ever worked the night shift?
Have you ever worked a night shift?
exercises.tip: worked es regular. «De noche» es at night.

exercises.es: Él ha estado en Londres dos veces.
exercises.answer: He has been to London twice.
exercises.tip: Ya volvió: been. Y «dos veces» es twice.

exercises.audio: Have you ever tried Colombian coffee?
exercises.meaning: ¿Alguna vez has probado café colombiano?
exercises.tip: try → tried, con i.

exercises.text: I have never been there.
exercises.tip: there con la th sonora. No es «der».

exercises.text: Have you ever been to London?
exercises.tip: Suena casi «hav-yu-EV-er bin tu LON-don». been aquí se dice corto, «bin».

exercises.es: Mi hermano se fue a Bogotá y todavía no ha vuelto.
exercises.answer: My brother has gone to Bogota.
accept: My brother's gone to Bogota.
My brother went to Bogota.
My brother has gone to Bogota and hasn't come back yet.
My brother went to Bogota and hasn't come back yet.
My brother has gone to Bogota and hasn't returned yet.
My brother went to Bogota and hasn't returned yet.
My brother has left for Bogota.
My brother left for Bogota.
My brother has gone to Bogota and he hasn't come back yet.
My brother went to Bogota and he hasn't come back yet.
My brother has gone to Bogota and hasn't come back.
My brother went to Bogota and hasn't come back.
My brother has gone to Bogota and still hasn't come back.
My brother went to Bogota and still hasn't come back.
My brother has gone to Bogota and is still there.
My brother went to Bogota and is still there.
exercises.tip: gone = se fue y sigue allá.

exercises.es: Nunca he estado en Nueva York.
exercises.answer: I have never been to New York.
accept: I have never been in New York.
I have never visited New York.
I have never gone to New York.
I never went to New York.
I have not been to New York.
I have never been to NYC.
I have never been to New York City.
I have never been to New York before.
I never visited New York.
I have never been in NYC.
exercises.tip: been to = fui y volví: la experiencia de haber estado.

exercises.text: Have you ever eaten arepas? Yes, I ___.
exercises.tip: La respuesta corta repite el ayudante: Yes, I have / No, I haven't. Es más natural que contestar con el verbo.

exercises.text: Yes, I have. Have you?
exercises.tip: La h de have se sopla suave, como un suspiro; no es la j fuerte del español.

theory.title: yet, already, just, still
theory.body:
Cuatro palabras que cambian de sitio según la frase.

**already** = ya (antes de lo esperado) — va **en el medio**
*I've **already** finished.*

**yet** = todavía / ya — solo en negativo y pregunta, **al final**
*I haven't finished **yet**.* · *Have you finished **yet**?*

**just** = acabo de — **en el medio**
*She has **just** left.*

**still** = todavía (sigue igual) — antes del verbo principal, pero después de am/is/are; en negativo, antes del auxiliar
*I **still** live here.* · *I'm **still** waiting.* · *I **still** haven't eaten.*

En inglés americano también se oye el **pasado simple** con just, already y yet: *I just arrived.* · *I already ate.* · *Did you eat yet?* Las dos formas son correctas.
theory.trap: «Acabo de llegar» se traduce solo con *just*: *I have **just** arrived*. No existe un verbo «acabar de» en inglés — *I finish to arrive* ❌ no significa nada.

accept: I just arrived.
I just got here.
I have just gotten here.
exercises.tip: «Acabar de» es just, metido entre have y el participio.

exercises.audio: I haven't finished yet.
exercises.tip: yet va al final, y solo en negativo o pregunta.

exercises.text: I have ___ eaten, thank you.
exercises.tip: already va entre have y el participio.

accept: She's just left.
She just left.
She has just gone out.
She just went out.
exercises.tip: El participio de leave es left.

exercises.answer: I am still waiting for the bus.
accept: I am still waiting for the bus to come.
exercises.tip: still va después de am y antes del -ing. Y esperar algo es wait for.

exercises.answer: Have you spoken to him yet?
exercises.tip: El participio de speak es spoken. En pregunta va yet, al final.

exercises.audio: They have already left.
exercises.meaning: Ellos ya se fueron.
exercises.tip: already, todo junto.

exercises.text: I have just gotten home.
exercises.tip: have y home con la h soplada.

exercises.text: I haven't finished yet.
exercises.tip: «haven't» se pega: «HAV-nt». El peso en FIN-ished.

theory.title: La pregunta que decide: ¿dices CUÁNDO?
theory.body:
Es la duda más grande del nivel, y hay una regla que casi nunca falla:

**Si la frase dice cuándo pasó → pasado simple.**
*I **ate** sushi **yesterday**.* · *She **went** to Paris **in 2020**.*

**Si no dice cuándo, y lo que importa es el resultado → present perfect.**
*I'**ve eaten** sushi.* (alguna vez) · *She'**s gone** to Paris.* (no está)

Palabras que **obligan** al pasado simple: *yesterday, last week, in 2020, ago, when I was young*.
Palabras que piden present perfect: *ever, never, already, yet, just, so far*. (En inglés americano, con just, already, yet y ever también se oye el pasado simple: *I just ate*, *Did you ever go?*)

Y para algo que **empezó antes y sigue hoy**: present perfect con **for** + duración (*for three years*) o **since** + punto de inicio (*since 2020*).
*I've lived here **for** three years.* · *I've known her **since** 2020.*
theory.trap: *I have eaten sushi yesterday* ❌ es el error insignia. En español «he comido sushi ayer» se oye normal; en inglés es imposible: si dices **yesterday**, el verbo tiene que ser **ate**.

accept: Yesterday I ate sushi.
I had sushi yesterday.
Yesterday I had sushi.
exercises.tip: yesterday dice cuándo, así que va pasado simple.

exercises.audio: She went to Paris in 2020.
options: She has gone to Paris in 2020.
She has been to Paris in 2020.
exercises.tip: Con in 2020 (un momento ya cerrado) va pasado simple. Ojo: con since 2020 sí va present perfect.

exercises.text: Have you ever ___ your passport?
exercises.tip: El participio de lose es lost, igual que el pasado.

exercises.es: Vi esa película la semana pasada.
exercises.answer: I saw that movie last week.
accept: I watched that movie last week.
I saw that film last week.
I watched that film last week.
Last week I saw that movie.
Last week I saw that film.
Last week I watched that movie.
Last week I watched that film.
exercises.tip: last week dice cuándo: pasado simple, saw.

exercises.answer: I have lived here for three years.
accept: I have been living here for three years.
I have lived here three years.
I have been living here three years.
exercises.tip: Sigue siendo verdad hoy: present perfect. Y una duración lleva for.

accept: In 2019 he worked here.
exercises.tip: Con el año, pasado simple.

exercises.audio: I have known her since 2020.
accept: I have known her since twenty twenty.
exercises.meaning: La conozco desde 2020.
exercises.tip: since para un punto de inicio; for para una duración.

exercises.text: I have lived here for three years.
exercises.tip: three con la lengua entre los dientes.

exercises.text: I ate sushi yesterday.
exercises.tip: Frase corta y seca. El peso en SU-shi y en YES-terday.
La diferencia está en la vocal: since lleva la i corta; sense lleva una e clara. El final suena igual en las dos.

units.title: Desde cuándo y lo que pudiste
units.subtitle: for, since, How long…? y could / was able to

theory.title: for y since: lo que empezó y sigue
theory.body:
Para algo que **empezó en el pasado y sigue hoy**, el inglés usa el present perfect, no el presente.

**for** + cuánto tiempo: *for ten years, for two weeks*
**since** + el momento en que empezó: *since 2016, since Monday, since I was a kid*
«Desde hace diez años» = **for** ten years (❌ *since ten years*).

*I**'ve lived** here **for** ten years.* · *I**'ve lived** here **since** 2016.*
***How long have you** worked there?* = ¿Hace cuánto trabajas ahí?

Si ya terminó, va pasado simple: *I **lived** in Cali **for** two years.* (ya no vivo allá)

Y **ago** va con pasado simple: *I **moved** here ten years **ago**.*
theory.trap: «Vivo aquí desde 2016» y «llevo diez años aquí» están en presente, y salen ❌ *I live here since 2016* y ❌ *I am here for ten years*; y «desde hace» sale ❌ *since two years*. Si empezó antes y sigue, va **have + participio**: **I've lived here since 2016**, **I've been here for ten years**. Y el «hace» de «llegué hace diez años» es **ago**, con pasado simple: *I came here ten years ago*.

accept: I've lived here since twenty sixteen.
I've been living here since 2016.
I've been living here since twenty sixteen.
I've been here since 2016.
I've been here since twenty sixteen.
I've lived here since two thousand sixteen.
I've been here since two thousand sixteen.
exercises.tip: Empezó en 2016 y sigue: have + participio + since.

exercises.audio: How long have you worked there?
options: How long do you work there?
How long have you worked there?
exercises.answer: How long have you worked there?
exercises.tip: ¿Hace cuánto…? = How long have you + participio?

exercises.es: Trabajo en este banco desde marzo.
exercises.text: I've worked at this bank ___ March.
exercises.tip: March es el momento en que empezó: since.

exercises.es: Conozco a Ana desde hace cinco años.
exercises.answer: I've known Ana for five years.
accept: I've known Ana five years.
I met Ana five years ago.
I've known Ana for the past five years.
I've known Ana for the last five years.
exercises.tip: «Conozco desde hace» = I've known… for. know casi nunca va en -ing.

exercises.audio: She moved to Miami two years ago.
options: She moved to Miami two years ago.
She has moved to Miami since two years.
She moves to Miami for two years.
exercises.answer: She moved to Miami two years ago.
exercises.tip: ago = hace, y va con pasado simple: moved.

exercises.text: I've lived in this city for three years.
exercises.tip: I've y lived terminan en v: dientes de arriba sobre el labio de abajo. No es «aib libd».

accept: I've been married since twenty fifteen.
I got married in 2015.
I got married in twenty fifteen.
I've been married since two thousand fifteen.
I got married in two thousand fifteen.
exercises.tip: Estar casado = be married. Desde 2015 y sigue: have been married since.

exercises.answer: How long have you had your car?
exercises.tip: have + had es normal: have es el ayudante y had el participio de have.

exercises.es: Viví en Cali dos años (ya no vivo allá).
exercises.text: I lived in Cali ___ two years.
exercises.tip: Ya terminó: pasado simple. Pero la duración sigue siendo for.

exercises.sentence: She has lived here for fifteen years.
exercises.tip: fifteen lleva el acento al final, «fif-TEEN», y una n. fifty lo lleva al principio, «FIF-ty».

exercises.audio: We haven't seen each other since Christmas.
exercises.meaning: No nos vemos desde Navidad.
exercises.tip: since + el momento: since Christmas. Y no nos vemos = haven't seen each other.

exercises.answer: How long have you lived in this apartment?
accept: How long have you been living in this apartment?
How long have you lived in this apartment for?
How long have you been in this apartment?
How long have you been living in this apartment for?
How long have you been in this apartment for?
exercises.tip: Vives ahí todavía: How long have you lived…?, no How long do you live…?

exercises.text: How long have you been here? For about two years.
exercises.tip: «how long» va pegado y sube en LONG. been se dice corto: «bin».

theory.title: could y was able to
theory.body:
**could** es el pasado de can: sirve para una **habilidad general** en el pasado. Como can, **no cambia y no lleva to**.

*I **could** swim when I was six.*
*My dad **couldn't** read English.*

Para **un logro concreto**, una vez y con esfuerzo, se usa **was/were able to** o **managed to**:
*The door was stuck, but I **was able to** open it.*
*We **managed to** find a taxi.*

En negativo, **couldn't** sirve para los dos casos: *I **couldn't** open the door.*

Excepción: con see, hear y understand, could sí sirve para una vez: *I **could** see the ocean.*
theory.trap: «Podía» y «pude» salen igual en español, y aparecen ❌ *I could to go*, ❌ *I can swim when I was a child* (can es presente) y ❌ *Finally I could open the door* para un logro de una sola vez. Con **could** el verbo va desnudo, y para «por fin pude» lo natural es **I was able to open it**.

exercises.es: Podía nadar cuando tenía seis años.
options: I can swim when I was six.
I could to swim when I was six.
I could swim when I was six.
exercises.answer: I could swim when I was six.
accept: I could swim when I was six years old.
I was able to swim when I was six.
I was able to swim when I was six years old.
I knew how to swim when I was six.
I knew how to swim when I was six years old.
exercises.tip: Habilidad general en el pasado: could + verbo desnudo. Y la edad va con was.

exercises.audio: I couldn't find my keys.
options: I didn't could find my keys.
exercises.tip: couldn't: la l no suena, se dice «KUD-nt». No usa did.

exercises.es: Por fin pude abrir la puerta.
exercises.text: Finally, I was ___ to open the door.
exercises.tip: Un logro de una vez: was able to.

accept: My grandma couldn't read.
My grandmother didn't know how to read.
My grandma didn't know how to read.
My grandmother wasn't able to read.
My grandma wasn't able to read.
exercises.tip: «Saber» + verbo, como habilidad, es can/could: couldn't read.

exercises.text: I couldn't hear the teacher.
exercises.tip: hear con la h soplada, no «ear». Y en couldn't la l no se pronuncia.

exercises.answer: We managed to find a taxi.
exercises.tip: managed to = logramos, con esfuerzo. Después de to, el verbo desnudo: find.

accept: Last night I couldn't sleep.
I wasn't able to sleep last night.
Last night I wasn't able to sleep.
I couldn't fall asleep last night.
Last night I couldn't fall asleep.
I couldn't get to sleep last night.
I couldn't get any sleep last night.
Last night I couldn't get to sleep.
I wasn't able to fall asleep last night.
Last night I wasn't able to fall asleep.
I couldn't sleep at all last night.
exercises.tip: En negativo, couldn't sirve para cualquier «no pude».

exercises.audio: She was able to pass the test.
options: She was able to pass the test.
exercises.answer: She was able to pass the test.
exercises.tip: Pasar un examen concreto es un logro de una vez: was able to.

exercises.audio: When I was young, I could run really fast.
exercises.meaning: Cuando era joven, podía correr muy rápido.
exercises.tip: could para lo que sabías hacer en general. fast no lleva -ly.

exercises.es: Mi hermano podía tocar la guitarra a los diez años.
exercises.text: My brother ___ play the guitar when he was ten.
accept: was able to
knew how to
exercises.tip: Habilidad general: could, sin to detrás.

exercises.sentence: I couldn't walk for two weeks.
exercises.tip: walk no tiene r y suena «wok»; work lleva r y suena «werk».

exercises.answer: Were you able to talk to your boss?
accept: Were you able to talk with your boss?
Were you able to speak to your boss?
Were you able to speak with your boss?
Did you manage to talk to your boss?
Did you manage to talk with your boss?
Did you manage to speak to your boss?
Did you manage to speak with your boss?
Did you get to talk to your boss?
Did you get to talk with your boss?
Did you get to speak to your boss?
Did you get to speak with your boss?
Did you get a chance to talk to your boss?
Did you get a chance to talk with your boss?
Did you get a chance to speak to your boss?
Did you get a chance to speak with your boss?
exercises.tip: Una ocasión concreta: Were you able to…?. Ojo: Could you talk to your boss? se entiende como «¿podrías hablar con tu jefe?».

exercises.text: The door was stuck, but I was able to open it.
exercises.tip: «was able to» sale rápido: «wəz-EI-bəl-tə». El peso cae en O de open.

units.title: Obligación y consejo
units.subtitle: have to, must y should — y la trampa de mustn't

theory.title: have to: la obligación de afuera
theory.body:
**have to** = tener que. La obligación viene de fuera: el trabajo, la ley, el horario.

*I **have to** work on Saturday.*
*She **has to** wear a uniform.*

Se comporta como un verbo normal, así que usa **do/does** y **did**:
*I **don't have to** go.* · ***Do** you **have to** work?*
*I **had to** wait two hours.* (pasado)

Y lo que sigue lleva **to**: *have **to** work*.
theory.trap: **don't have to** no significa «no debes»: significa **no es necesario**. *You don't have to come* es «no es necesario que vengas», no «no vengas». El «no debes» es otra palabra, y va en la lección siguiente.

options: I must to work on Saturday.
I have to work on Saturday.
exercises.answer: I have to work on Saturday.
accept: I have to work this Saturday.
I need to work on Saturday.
I have got to work on Saturday.
I have work on Saturday.
I have to work Saturday.
exercises.tip: have to + verbo. Y los días con on.

exercises.audio: She has to wear a uniform.
options: She had to wear a uniform.
She has to wear a uniform.
She has to wears a uniform.
